Write-up:
# Dense high-girth components with an all-orders padding argument

Problem: TOP-30006856  
Claim type: Literature report  
Author: /root/hundred_graphs

**Exact scope.** For every fixed integer k≥4, put
\[
 d_k=\left\lceil\frac{3(k-1)}2\right\rceil.
\]
For all \(n\ge4\cdot2^{d_k}\), there is a simple n-vertex graph with girth greater than2k and
\[
 |E|\ge 2^{-3-2/d_k}\,n^{1+1/d_k}. \tag{1}
\]
The algebraic construction is the credited Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar theorem [1]. We give its precise parameters and prove the all-n deduction even though the selected connected component's exact order need not be known. This classical bound is not presented as a new or current-best exponent.

The previous A1 supplies explicit sharp k=2 and k=3 families and a general random-alteration exponent \(1+1/(2k-1)\). The bound (1) has a larger exponent for every k≥4 because \(d_k<2k-1\). It remains short of the conjectured \(1+1/k\) for k≥4, and the famous exceptional sharp k=5 construction is not being re-proved here.

We use the following exact external input from [1, Proposition2.1, Lemma3.1 and Theorem3.2]. For an odd integer L≥3 and a prime power q, let
\[
 t=\left\lfloor\frac{L+2}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The paper defines a simple bipartite q-regular graph \(D(L,q)\) with \(2q^L\) vertices. Its girth is at least L+5. Its automorphisms are transitive on each bipartition class and on edges, so its connected components are isomorphic. If their number is \(N_{L,q}\), the paper proves
\[
 N_{L,q}\ge q^{t-1}.
\]
Accordingly any component \(C=CD(L,q)\) is simple, bipartite, connected and q-regular, and has
\[
 v=|V(C)|=\frac{2q^L}{N_{L,q}}
       \le2q^{L-t+1},\qquad
 \operatorname{girth}(C)\ge L+5,\qquad
 |E(C)|=\frac{vq}{2}. \tag{2}
\]
There is no need here for an equality formula for \(N_{L,q}\), nor for the source's extra congruence condition giving equality of girth.

For orientation, the component bound is not obtained by arbitrarily discarding vertices from a dense graph. The source uses polynomial invariants constant along edges to exhibit at least \(q^{t-1}\) distinct component labels. Component transitivity then converts their count into the order bound in (2). This invariant/transitivity argument is part of the credited algebraic theorem; no implementation or independent reproduction of its full coordinate calculation is claimed.

Set \(L=2k-3\). Then L is odd and at least5, and (2) gives girth at least
\[
 L+5=2k+2>2k.
\]
The exponent in its order bound is exactly
\[
 L-t+1
 =2k-2-\left\lfloor\frac{2k-1}{4}\right\rfloor
 =\left\lceil\frac{3(k-1)}2\right\rceil=d_k. \tag{3}
\]
For example k=4,5,6,7 give d=5,6,8,9 respectively. Both parity cases follow directly from writing k=2r or k=2r+1.

Here is the padding step, with no unjustified assumption that component orders occur at bounded ratios. Given n as above, choose the largest power of two q with
\[
 4q^{d_k}\le n.
\]
Then q≥2 and
\[
 q>\frac12(n/4)^{1/d_k}. \tag{4}
\]
Take any component C from (2). Its unknown order v satisfies \(v\le2q^{d_k}\le n/2\). Form \(s=\lfloor n/v\rfloor\) disjoint copies of C, and add \(n-sv\) isolated vertices. This is a simple graph on exactly n vertices. Every cycle belongs to one component, so its girth is still at least2k+2. Since \(n/v\ge2\), we have \(s\ge n/(2v)\). Thus
\[
 |E|=\frac{svq}{2}\ge\frac{nq}{4}
 >2^{-3-2/d_k}n^{1+1/d_k},
\]
by (4), proving (1).

This step is useful because an upper bound \(v\le2q^{d_k}\) alone does not justify replacing v by an arbitrary n in the component's edge expression. If v were much smaller than its upper bound, adding isolated vertices to just one copy could lose density. Taking enough disjoint copies retains total degree mass of order nq. No connectedness is required in the literal conjecture.

For comparison with the target, \(d_k\) is asymptotic to \(3k/2\), rather than k. The construction supplies roughly \(n^{1+2/(3k)}\) edges, while the prompt requests \(n^{1+1/k}\). These exponent statements cannot be made equivalent by changing constants that depend only on k. For k=4 the present exponent is6/5, short of5/4; for k=6 it is9/8, short of7/6.

The source is a historical primary construction. No claim that its exponent is the strongest available in2026 is needed, and its introduction's historical “best known” language is not imported as a current status assertion. The contribution adds a verified substantial general construction to the earlier elementary bounds, identifies the exact unproved conjectural gap, and supplies an explicit uniform all-orders conversion. No finite graph test is presented as proof of the infinite construction.

[1] F. Lazebnik, V. A. Ustimenko and A. J. Woldar, *A New Series of Dense Graphs of High Girth*, author-hosted primary manuscript, Proposition2.1, Lemma3.1 and Theorem3.2, https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/3/7714/files/2022/02/bullfin1.pdf .
